approach.method_basis: This node transfers MAX-MIN Ant System, a classical ant colony optimiser, onto molecular graph building. Every proposed molecule is constructed from nothing: an ant picks a starting atom, then repeatedly either attaches a new atom by a chosen bond to some existing atom, closes a ring bond between two atoms already present, or stops, with valence rules deciding which moves are legal at each step. The probability of each legal move is a fixed chemical heuristic weight, read off aggregate frequencies in an unlabeled corpus, multiplied by a learned pheromone weight. The crucial choice is what the pheromone is indexed by: not the molecule being built and not the sequence so far, but a small local description of the attachment site together with the move's own atom and bond attributes, so the same pheromone entry is consulted whenever that local situation recurs in any molecule. After each batch of proposals is scored, all pheromone weights evaporate by a fixed fraction, only the single best-scoring accepted molecule in that batch deposits reinforcement, and it deposits only on the entries its own construction actually used. Every weight is then clipped into a fixed positive interval, the max-min part of the method, so no move is ever driven to zero probability and no move ever takes over completely. The bet is that a local decision that helped once will help again in a structurally different molecule.
approach.novelty: The method statement says pheromones are keyed by solution components; for molecules that leaves the most important design decision open, and this root answers it concretely. Keys combine a bounded local attachment environment, made of atom identity, charge, hydrogen count, degree, bond-order sum and ring membership, with the candidate move's own attributes, and ring-closure keys additionally carry both endpoint environments and a path-length class. Keys are explicitly forbidden from encoding a whole prefix, a whole partial graph, or any observation identifier, which is what separates this from a prefix tree and makes credit genuinely shareable across unrelated partial molecules. The remaining commitments are all fixed in advance and identical across objectives: pheromone exponent 1.5 against heuristic exponent 1, evaporation of 0.18 per update, weights clipped to the interval from 0.025 to 1, and one rank-scaled deposit per distinct key on the winner's trace rather than one per repeated occurrence. The corpus is used only for aggregate atom, bond, ring-closure and stopping frequencies, published as tables with no molecule library retained anywhere. Pheromones start broad and are seeded by exactly replaying the construction of the single highest-scoring supplied molecule, then every objective gets its own fresh table. Only accepted whole-molecule feedback moves anything: invalid, duplicate, rejected and still-pending constructions never deposit. The node also deliberately restricts itself to each ant's own generating trace, holding back the idea of spreading one molecule's score across its equivalent construction orders as a separate later experiment.

observed_bottleneck: This root has no Parent. Sparse whole-molecule feedback must guide many local structural decisions without repeatedly evaluating the same molecules. The supplied observation n-b9659a6161cd confirms that a sequential prefix-tree method used accepted returns in subsequent choices and reports concentrated rollout-start prefixes. This motivates testing local graph-context actions as a different location for reusable feedback. It does not establish an ant-colony failure, prove that prefix concentration caused poor scores, or show that local action credit will transfer usefully. The untested prerequisites are a viable corpus-informed construction grammar and sufficiently informative shared contexts under the supplied budget.
hypothesis: Construct each proposed molecule anew with valence-aware molecular graph actions sampled from fixed corpus-derived chemical heuristics times shared task-local bounded pheromones, then evaporate all pheromones and reinforce only the accepted batch-best molecule's actual construction trace so successful local actions guide later ants across different partial graphs.

finding_summary.headline: Shared construction credit spread almost everywhere yet improved almost nothing; 0.2523, eleventh of twelve scored roots
finding_summary.insights: The campaign now has a clean separation between credit spreading and credit being useful. This root demonstrates that local-context pheromones do transfer: 70,235 selected moves reused a winner's reinforcement inside a structurally different partial molecule, with 70,175 of those reuses occurring at a different atom count entirely, so the mechanism is not a disguised prefix tree. But nearly every accepted ant inherited that bias while almost none benefited from it, which says the local key is too coarse to be selective. A context of atom identity, degree, hydrogens and ring membership recurs so often that reinforcing it nudges essentially the whole colony in the same direction rather than steering it toward the winner's chemistry. Against the twelve scored Discovery roots, whose macro means span 0.2331 to 0.5103, this root's 0.2523 ranks eleventh, in the bottom third and only marginally above the weakest root; the honest reading is that ant colony optimisation at this credit resolution is not competitive here. Two things stay open. The root deliberately deferred spreading a winner's score across the equivalent construction orders of the same molecule, which is the obvious way to make each accepted score inform more contexts, and it has not tested whether a richer key, or a deposit weighted by how distinctive a context is, would make credit selective. It is also a single seed with no parent and no ablation, so nothing here isolates the pheromone contribution from the fixed corpus heuristic that was doing the rest of the work.
finding_summary.results: Macro mean was 0.2523 on the single screening seed, with per-task final Top-1 of 0.5534 on the decoration-hopping objective, 0.3051 on the zaleplon multi-property objective, 0.1678 on the second median-molecule objective, 0.1371 on the dopamine-receptor docking objective and 0.0980 on the sitagliptin multi-property objective. The machinery worked in full. The construction grammar exactly replayed 39,545 of 40,000 sampled corpus molecules, a rate of 0.9886, and exactly replayed all 50 supplied starting molecules. The colony then built 1,450 molecules in 145 batches of ten, every one valid and connected, with zero invalid retries, zero duplicates and zero evaluator rejections; 77,416 construction actions were taken and 1,168 of the products were cyclic. Pheromone updates were exact in all 145 online events, always reinforcing the true highest accepted score, and probability mass genuinely shifted: 6,558 of 6,633 competitive probes increased the reinforced key's share, mean signed shift +0.0193, with 67 unchanged and 8 slightly reduced by the lower clipping bound. Sharing was real and extensive, with 71,453 selected reuses of reinforced moves in different partial molecules, 70,235 of them traceable to online feedback. The payoff did not follow. Of 1,399 accepted ants that reused online-reinforced components, only 3 beat their pre-batch incumbent, a rate of 0.0021. Initial-to-final incumbent improvements were 0, 0.00497, 0.1181, 0 and 0.0959 across the five objectives, so on two objectives no constructed molecule ever beat a supplied starting molecule, and on the decoration-hopping objective the entire 0.005 gain arrived in the first generated batch, before any online deposition could have steered it.

molecular.headline: Long conjugated polyene chains and strained fused cages, with aromatic rings largely absent from the output
molecular.overall_character: The colony builds large, heavily unsaturated, mostly non-aromatic molecules. Mean SMILES length runs 74 to 87 characters on every objective with maxima of 113 to 127, and the constructions averaged around 50 atoms, far beyond ordinary small-molecule size. Aromatic atoms appear in only 20 to 42 percent of the emitted strings, which is the defining deficiency: rings that do form are usually written as non-aromatic C=C closures, strained fused cages, or bridged polycyclics carrying exocyclic quinoid double bonds onto ring atoms. Ring formation itself is inconsistent, present in 95 to 97 percent of strings on three objectives but only 55 to 61 percent on the other two, where the output degenerates into unbranched polyene chains 90 to 110 characters long, alternating C=C with occasional methyl branches and almost no heteroatoms. Nitrogen, when it appears, is nearly always a chain imine or enamine rather than a ring nitrogen. Stereochemistry is entirely absent across all 1,450 constructions. The overall impression is of a valence-correct graph builder that has learned atom and bond frequencies without learning what a molecule is shaped like.

per_task.generated_character: The weakest chemistry of the five. Ring closures appear in only 61 percent of strings and aromatic atoms in 22 percent, while mean length is 76.2. Most molecules are long alternating polyene chains with methyl branches; the minority that close rings produce strained fused cages with amide or nitrile groups buried inside them.
liabilities: unbranched conjugated polyene chains of twenty or more sp2 carbons, which are not isolable compounds
bridged spiro cages with multiple fused three and four membered rings
exocyclic quinoid double bonds drawn onto ring atoms, giving non-Kekulisable-looking systems
missing_features: any fused nitrogen heteroaromatic bicycle, which the colony never constructs on this objective
aromatic rings at all in roughly four fifths of the proposals
compact molecules of drug-like size; the outputs average more than twice the length of the supplied starting molecules
discrete polar functional groups such as a simple amide on an aromatic ring rather than nitrogen buried in a cage
per_task.score_gradient_reading: More than half of all proposals scored exactly 0, since the median of the read molecules is 0.0. The handful that scored at all, up to 0.1776, are the compact cyclic ones carrying nitrogen and a nitrile; the zero band is uniformly the 90 to 110 character polyene chains. Decisively, no constructed molecule ever beat a supplied starting molecule here, so the reported final Top-1 of 0.3051 is that starting molecule's own score and not something the colony built.

per_task.generated_character: The largest molecules of the five, mean SMILES length 86.0 with a maximum of 126 and ring closures in 94 percent of strings, yet aromatic atoms in only 42 percent. The high-scoring band is dominated by enormous fused polycyclic systems, often ten or more rings, decorated with enamines, imines, formamides and long alkenyl tails, at a size and complexity no synthesis could reach.
liabilities: fused polycyclic assemblies exceeding one hundred characters with no synthetic route implied
extended enamine and imine ladders as the main nitrogen chemistry
exocyclic double bonds written onto aromatic ring atoms throughout the high-scoring band
missing_features: an aromatic amide-linked biaryl core, which the outputs approximate only with non-aromatic fused carbocycles
sulfonamide, sulfone or comparable discrete polar linkers, essentially absent from the emitted set
any control of molecular size; the outputs are several times larger than the supplied starting molecules
clean substitution patterns on a single ring rather than nitrogen and oxygen scattered through a fused mass
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The scoring floor on this objective is 0.5 and almost everything lands within a few hundredths of it, from 0.5 to 0.5534. Larger molecules with more nitrogen and more ring closures sit at the top of that narrow band and short alkene fragments sit at the bottom, but the separation is only about 0.05 in total. The best constructed molecule at 0.5534 improved on the best supplied starting molecule at 0.5484 by 0.005, and that entire gain arrived in the first generated batch.

per_task.generated_character: Ring closures in 97 percent of strings but aromatic atoms in only 29 percent, mean length 85.6. The best molecules are tightly fused polycyclic cages with a ketone and an exocyclic quinoid ring, the middle of the distribution is long polyene chains threaded through occasional partially saturated rings, and the bottom is short acyclic aldehyde and thioether fragments.
liabilities: densely fused cage systems with bridgehead alkenes that violate normal strain limits
long conjugated polyene chains carrying isolated rings as decoration
exocyclic quinoid bonds onto aromatic rings in the highest-scoring molecule
missing_features: a basic protonatable amine on a saturated ring, absent from the emitted molecules
aromatic heterocycles such as pyridine or indole as ring building blocks
a simple two to four atom linker joining two distinct aromatic ends
molecules small enough to fit a binding site; mean size here is roughly double a typical ligand
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Score climbs with ring count and with nitrogen inside rings rather than in chains: the top molecule at 0.1371 is a compact fused cage with two ring nitrogens, while the 0.0289 plateau that many molecules share is polyene chemistry with a couple of loose rings attached. The colony genuinely improved here, from a best supplied starting molecule at 0.0190 to 0.1371, the largest gain it achieved on any objective.

per_task.generated_character: Ring closures in 95 percent of strings, aromatic atoms in 31 percent, branching in every single molecule, mean length 87.4, the longest of the five. Typical outputs are large partially saturated fused polycyclics bearing aldehydes, enones and lactams, plus a long alkenyl or aminoalkyl tail.
liabilities: bridged polycyclic cages with quaternary bridgeheads and multiple exocyclic alkenes
N-oxide and nitro groups placed on strained ring systems
polyene chains bearing aldehyde and nitrile termini in the low-scoring band
missing_features: a methylenedioxyphenyl or comparable fused dioxole ring, never constructed here
sulfonamide-bearing saturated nitrogen heterocycles
aromatic rings in roughly seven tenths of the proposals
compact molecules; the outputs are far larger than the supplied starting molecules and grow rather than converge
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The best band, 0.108 to 0.131, is consistently the fused polycyclic lactams and quinone-like systems; the worst band, 0.010 to 0.019, is acyclic polyene and polyketone chains with no ring system. As on the zaleplon objective, nothing the colony built beat a supplied starting molecule, so the reported final Top-1 of 0.1678 belongs to a starting molecule and the best construction reached only 0.1310.

per_task.generated_character: Ring closures in only 55 percent of strings and aromatic atoms in 20 percent, the lowest of the five, with mean length 74.2. The output is overwhelmingly acyclic: long unsaturated chains carrying esters, aldehydes, enones, amides and secondary amines, with only a minority closing any ring at all.
liabilities: unbranched conjugated polyene chains of 100 characters or more dominating the zero-scoring band
stacked Michael acceptors, with multiple enones and enals on one chain
thioether and thioaldehyde fragments appended to already unstable chains
missing_features: trifluoromethyl groups and polyfluorinated aromatic rings, essentially never constructed
fused bicyclic heteroaromatic amine cores of the triazolopyrazine type
saturated nitrogen heterocycles rather than chain amines and imines
a beta-amino amide arrangement placing a primary amine beta to a carbonyl
rings at all in nearly half the emitted molecules
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The median score is 0.0 and the worst is 0.0, so most proposals were valueless. The few that scored, up to 0.0980, are the shortest and most ring-bearing, pairing a lactone or cyclopentanone with a primary amine or enamine; every long chain scored zero or near zero. The best construction did beat the best supplied starting molecule at 0.0021, so the relative gain is large while the absolute level stays very low, and the final batch fell back to between 1e-13 and 0.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Aromatic atoms appear in only 20 to 42 percent of emitted molecules across all five objectives, against 55 to 97 percent that carry some ring closure. Rings that do form are written as non-aromatic alternating C=C closures or as strained fused cages, and the supplied starting molecules, which are aromatic throughout, are far more aromatic than anything the generator builds.
transferable_gaps.gap: Aromatic ring systems are barely reachable by this construction process
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A construction grammar that builds rings one bond at a time will only reach aromatic systems by accident unless aromatic rings are available as whole units. The generator needs closure moves that commit to a complete aromatic ring, or a fragment vocabulary containing common aromatic rings, rather than requiring the search to assemble six correct bonds in sequence.

transferable_gaps.evidence: On two objectives more than half of the proposals scored zero and the zero band is uniformly 90 to 110 character strings of alternating C=C with methyl branches and almost no heteroatoms. The same chain motif persists into the final proposals rather than being bred out over the run.
transferable_gaps.gap: The dominant output motif is a long unbranched conjugated chain, not a molecule
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Chain extension is being selected far more often than closure or termination because it is always legal. The generator needs its stopping and closure moves weighted against the growing cost of the chain, or a hard cap on consecutive unsaturated chain extensions, so that proposals cannot degenerate into polymers.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Mean SMILES length ranges 74 to 87 characters on every objective with maxima of 113 to 127, and the constructions averaged around 50 atoms and reached 64. That is several times the size of the supplied starting molecules, and on every objective the largest outputs cluster at the bottom of the score range.
transferable_gaps.gap: Molecule size is not bounded by anything the search can feel
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: The generator needs an explicit size prior tied to the corpus it was built from, and a termination probability that rises with the current atom count, so that feedback about quality is not confounded with an unchecked drift toward larger structures.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Across the emitted molecules, nitrogen shows up overwhelmingly as chain imines, enamines and secondary amines strung along an unsaturated backbone, while saturated heterocycles such as piperidine, piperazine and morpholine are essentially absent even in the best-scoring band of every objective.
transferable_gaps.gap: Nitrogen and oxygen appear as chain functionality rather than as ring members
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Heteroatom placement and ring closure are being chosen independently, so heteroatoms rarely end up inside rings. The generator needs its ring-closure moves to be conditioned on the heteroatom pattern of the growing fragment, or needs saturated heterocycles available as intact building blocks.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The highest-scoring constructions on several objectives are bridged polycyclic cages with quaternary bridgeheads, multiple three and four membered fused rings, and exocyclic quinoid double bonds drawn onto ring atoms. These pass a valence check but are not species a chemist would attempt.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring fusion produces strained cages and non-standard valence patterns
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Valence admissibility is too weak a gate on ring closure. The generator should restrict closures to ring sizes and fusion patterns observed in its corpus and reject bridgehead and strain configurations, so that its highest-reward outputs remain in reachable chemical space.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The stereocentre rate is exactly 0.0 across all five objectives and all 1,450 constructions, and the preparation step itself discarded corpus examples carrying specified stereochemistry, isotopes and larger ring closures as unsupported.
transferable_gaps.gap: No stereochemistry can be expressed at all
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Any reward depending on three-dimensional configuration is unreachable by construction. Stereo descriptors have to be part of the action space and survive into the emitted structure, rather than being dropped when the grammar was derived.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Reinforced moves were reused inside structurally different partial molecules 71,453 times, and 1,399 accepted proposals inherited that reinforcement, yet only 3 of them beat their own pre-batch incumbent. Nearly the whole population received the same nudge and almost none of it converted into better chemistry.
transferable_gaps.gap: Shared credit is spread so widely that it stops being informative
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: When credit is keyed to a local description that recurs in almost every molecule, reinforcement acts as a global bias rather than as guidance. A generator sharing credit this way needs its context resolution scaled to how distinctive the context is, or a deposit weighted down for contexts that occur everywhere, so that reinforcement discriminates instead of drifting.

method_name: MAX-MIN Ant System over a molecular construction grammar
method_thesis: Anchor the method in MAX-MIN Ant System: construct solutions probabilistically from components, evaporate their pheromone weights, reinforce the iteration-best solution, and bound every pheromone weight away from zero and excessive dominance. [Stutzle and Hoos, Sections 2 and 4](https://www.cs.ubc.ca/~hoos/Publ/fgcs00.pdf) describe this mechanism. Our molecular adaptation constructs a fresh graph from an empty state through valence-aware atom, bond, ring-closure and termination actions. Choice probabilities combine a fixed chemical heuristic with task-local pheromones keyed by the local attachment context and action, allowing a useful action to transfer between different partial graphs. Preparation uses the permitted unlabeled corpus only for aggregate construction frequencies and stopping statistics. Initialize pheromones broadly, reconstruct valid construction traces for the supplied scored molecules, and use their best trace for the initial reinforcement. Generate the announced batch through complete new construction trajectories; only accepted whole-molecule feedback drives evaporation and reinforcement of that batch's best trace. Resample failed or duplicate constructions locally. There is no stored complete-molecule library, corpus ranking or fixed product enumeration. The hypothesis is that reusing successful local construction choices across new molecular combinations raises the mean of independent final Top-1 scores. Whether coarse construction contexts carry useful reward information quickly enough is unproven; pheromone concentration or validity alone is not success.

method_references.title: Thomas Stutzle and Holger H. Hoos. MAX-MIN Ant System. Future Generation Computer Systems 16(8), 889-914, 2000. Author-hosted near-final manuscript; Sections 2 and 4 describe probabilistic construction, best-ant reinforcement, evaporation and pheromone limits.
